overview.text: The lungs are pyramid-shaped, paired organs that are connected to the trachea by the right and left bronchi; on the inferior surface, the lungs are bordered by the diaphragm.
overview.label: 22.2 Gross Anatomy of the Lungs

overview.text: The right lung is shorter and wider than the left lung, and the left lung occupies a smaller volume than the right.
overview.label: 22.2 Gross Anatomy of the Lungs

overview.text: The apex of the lung is the superior region, whereas the base is the opposite region near the diaphragm.
overview.label: 22.2 Gross Anatomy of the Lungs

overview.text: The costal surface of the lung borders the ribs.
overview.label: 22.2 Gross Anatomy of the Lungs

overview.text: The mediastinal surface faces the midline.
overview.label: 22.2 Gross Anatomy of the Lungs

overview.text: The right lung consists of three lobes: the superior, middle, and inferior lobes.
overview.label: 22.2 Gross Anatomy of the Lungs

overview.text: The left lung consists of two lobes: the superior and inferior lobes.
overview.label: 22.2 Gross Anatomy of the Lungs

lobes.text: Each lung is composed of smaller units called lobes.
lobes.label: 22.2 Gross Anatomy of the Lungs

lobes.text: Fissures separate these lobes from each other.
lobes.label: 22.2 Gross Anatomy of the Lungs

lobes.text: The right lung consists of three lobes: the superior, middle, and inferior lobes.
lobes.label: 22.2 Gross Anatomy of the Lungs

lobes.text: The left lung consists of two lobes: the superior and inferior lobes.
lobes.label: 22.2 Gross Anatomy of the Lungs

segment.text: A bronchopulmonary segment is a division of a lobe, and each lobe houses multiple bronchopulmonary segments.
segment.label: 22.2 Gross Anatomy of the Lungs

segment.text: Each segment receives air from its own tertiary bronchus and is supplied with blood by its own artery.
segment.label: 22.2 Gross Anatomy of the Lungs

trachea.text: The trachea is formed by 16 to 20 stacked, C-shaped pieces of hyaline cartilage that are connected by dense connective tissue.
trachea.label: 22.1 Trachea

trachea.text: The esophagus borders the trachea posteriorly.
trachea.label: 22.1 Trachea

trachea.text: The trachea branches into the right and left primary bronchi at the carina.
trachea.label: 22.1 Bronchial Tree

mainbronchi.text: The trachea branches into the right and left primary bronchi at the carina.
mainbronchi.label: 22.1 Bronchial Tree

mainbronchi.text: Rings of cartilage, similar to those of the trachea, support the structure of the bronchi and prevent their collapse.
mainbronchi.label: 22.1 Bronchial Tree

mainbronchi.text: The primary bronchi enter the lungs at the hilum, a concave region where blood vessels, lymphatic vessels, and nerves also enter the lungs.
mainbronchi.label: 22.1 Bronchial Tree

btree.text: The bronchi continue to branch into a bronchial tree.
btree.label: 22.1 Bronchial Tree

btree.text: A bronchial tree (or respiratory tree) is the collective term used for these multiple-branched bronchi.
btree.label: 22.1 Bronchial Tree

btree.text: Each segment receives air from its own tertiary bronchus and is supplied with blood by its own artery.
btree.label: 22.2 Gross Anatomy of the Lungs

segart.text: The pulmonary artery branches multiple times as it follows the bronchi, and each branch becomes progressively smaller in diameter.
segart.label: 22.2 Blood Supply

segart.text: Each segment receives air from its own tertiary bronchus and is supplied with blood by its own artery.
segart.label: 22.2 Gross Anatomy of the Lungs

ptrunk.text: The pulmonary artery is an artery that arises from the pulmonary trunk and carries deoxygenated, arterial blood to the alveoli.
ptrunk.label: 22.2 Blood Supply

ptrunk.text: The pulmonary artery branches multiple times as it follows the bronchi, and each branch becomes progressively smaller in diameter.
ptrunk.label: 22.2 Blood Supply

veins.text: Once the blood is oxygenated, it drains from the alveoli by way of multiple pulmonary veins, which exit the lungs through the hilum.
veins.label: 22.2 Blood Supply

passage.text: The trachea branches into the right and left primary bronchi at the carina.
passage.label: 22.1 Bronchial Tree

passage.text: The primary bronchi enter the lungs at the hilum, a concave region where blood vessels, lymphatic vessels, and nerves also enter the lungs.
passage.label: 22.1 Bronchial Tree

passage.text: Each segment receives air from its own tertiary bronchus and is supplied with blood by its own artery.
passage.label: 22.2 Gross Anatomy of the Lungs

passage.text: The pulmonary artery is an artery that arises from the pulmonary trunk and carries deoxygenated, arterial blood to the alveoli.
passage.label: 22.2 Blood Supply

passage.text: The pulmonary artery branches multiple times as it follows the bronchi, and each branch becomes progressively smaller in diameter.
passage.label: 22.2 Blood Supply

passage.text: Once the blood is oxygenated, it drains from the alveoli by way of multiple pulmonary veins, which exit the lungs through the hilum.
passage.label: 22.2 Blood Supply
